title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
slides: Can Congress close the Nvidia backdoor?

thread_text:
1. The Nvidia backdoor question

Lawmakers want tighter export rules on AI chips after a spy scandal involved chips found in restricted hands. Congress is now asking if the backdoor can be closed.

2. Export rules under scrutiny

Companies exporting chips may face new license hurdles. The proposal targets AI chips specifically, aiming to prevent them from reaching restricted entities.

3. Spy scandal raises alarms

The scandal involved chips found in restricted hands, prompting lawmakers to demand stricter controls. This incident has accelerated calls for reform.

4. License hurdles ahead

If new rules pass, exporters will need licenses for AI chip sales. This could slow down shipments and increase compliance costs for companies.

5. Audit your supply chain now

Before rules land, audit your chip supply chain. Identify where your chips end up and ensure no restricted parties are receiving them. Start today.

instagram.caption:
Lawmakers want new license requirements before AI chips leave the country, after a spy scandal put restricted chips in the wrong hands.

Congress is asking whether the export backdoor can actually be closed.

Right now, exporters can ship AI chips under existing rules. If the proposal passes, each AI chip sale abroad could need a license first.

That means slower shipments and new compliance costs for anyone building with these chips.
